title: Thailand vs Indonesia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Thailand and Indonesia for Southeast Asia travelers, covering beaches, temples, food, costs, and travel logistics.

categories.title: 🍜 Food & Street Food

faqs.question: Is Thailand or Indonesia better for beaches?
faqs.answer: Both have world-class beaches, but they're different. Thailand's best beaches (Krabi, Koh Lanta, Koh Tao, the Similan Islands) are polished, accessible, and well-served by guesthouses and beach bars. faqs.question: Is Thailand or Indonesia cheaper?
faqs.answer: Indonesia (specifically Bali and Java) is marginally cheaper for budget travelers, but the difference narrows as you move upmarket. faqs.question: Is Thailand or Indonesia better for first-time Southeast Asia visitors?
faqs.answer: Thailand is the more accessible entry point. It has excellent transport infrastructure, widespread English, a very well-developed tourist trail, and easy navigation. faqs.question: Which has better street food — Thailand or Indonesia?
faqs.answer: Thailand wins on street food by most travelers' accounts. Bangkok's street food is legendary — pad thai, khao man gai, boat noodles, mango sticky rice, and hundreds of regional dishes available at stalls for $1-2. faqs.answer: Thailand: 7-10 days covers Bangkok, Chiang Mai, and one island group (Koh Samui area or Krabi/Koh Lanta). Two weeks lets you do north and south properly. faqs.question: Can you visit both Thailand and Indonesia in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes — very popular combination. Bangkok or Chiang Mai to Bali takes about 5-6 hours with one connection (or direct on some routes). faqs.answer: Indonesia wins for diving, and it's not close. Raja Ampat in West Papua is considered one of the top 3 dive sites in the world, with the highest marine biodiversity on Earth.
